transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I guess what brings me in is... well, I've been having a little trouble with my eating habits lately. It's honestly a bit embarrassing to talk about, so I hope I'm explaining it okay. But sometimes I, you know, overdo it a bit. And the thing that really bothers me is that after I do it, I just sit there looking at the empty containers and wrappers, and I feel so... disgusted with myself. 

I've always tried to be a steady, in-control kind of man, you know? I pride myself on that. But when I'm sitting there looking at the mess, I just don't feel like that man at all. Is... is that the kind of information you need to know?
After these episodes where you feel like you've overeaten, do you ever try to compensate for it by doing something like making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Oh, no, doctor. No, I don't do anything like that. I mean, making myself sick or... taking laxatives, no. I wouldn't do that. I just... well, I just kind of sit with the guilt, I guess. 

And with my job—I drive a truck for a living—I'm sitting behind the wheel most of the day, so I definitely don't have the time or energy to go exercising a lot more than usual. I just try to put it behind me and tell myself I'll do better the next day, even if I usually end up messing up again. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I know the overeating part is really bad, but I try to keep a level head and not do anything extreme like making myself sick afterward. Does that answer your question okay?

Can you describe how often these episodes of overeating happen, and do you feel like you're eating much more rapidly than normal, eating until you're uncomfortably full, or eating large amounts even when you're not hungry?

Well, doctor, I... I hope I'm answering this right. As far as eating fast or when I'm not hungry, I mean, maybe a little bit? I try to keep it together, so I wouldn't say I'm completely out of control or anything like that. I just eat until I'm done, mostly. I hope that makes sense. 

But as for how often it happens... well, it's a bit embarrassing to admit. I've been off the road and stuck at home lately with a back injury. And since I’ve been home with this injury, it’s... well, it's been happening several nights most weeks. Honestly, I can’t think of a single week in these past three months where I didn’t have at least one of those episodes. 

Being cooped up just really throws off my routine, I guess. I know it doesn't sound great, but I really am trying my best to manage it. Does that help? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
Do these episodes of overeating cause you significant distress, or have they affected your daily life, work, or relationships in any way?

Well, um... distress is a strong word, I think. I mean, I try not to let it get to me too much. But, honestly, I guess it has been bothering me a little more than I'd like to admit. 

As for my daily life, I’m mostly just dealing with my back, so I’m home anyway. But... well, there is one thing. At work, I'm supposed to mentor some of the newer drivers. We usually have these regular check-in calls. Lately, though, I've... I've kind of been avoiding them. I just feel so ashamed of myself, you know? I don't want them hearing it in my voice, how far off my routine I've gotten and how I'm not that steady guy they think I am. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad mentor. I really do care about the guys, I just... I want to get myself sorted out first so I can set a good example again. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
During these episodes of overeating, do you feel like you're losing control — like you can't stop eating or can't control what or how much you're eating?

Well, um... I guess "losing control" sounds a bit extreme, doctor. I mean, I'm usually a very disciplined guy. When I'm on the road, I run a tight ship. So I wouldn't say I completely lose my mind or anything like that. 

But... well, I suppose, lately, since I've been stuck at home... it does feel a little bit like that discipline just kind of shuts off. It's... it's really embarrassing to admit, actually. It's like, once I start, even while I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Magin, put the fork down, you don't need this,' my hand just... it just keeps going back for more. 

I try really hard to stop, I promise I do. It's just hard right now with everything being so out of whack. I hope you don't think less of me for that. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way.
Can you tell me if during these overeating episodes you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual, eating until you're uncomfortably full, or eating a lot even when you're not hungry?

Well, doctor, I know you brought this up earlier, and I... I think I kind of glossed over it because I didn't want to sound like I was totally off the rails. I hope you don't mind me backtracking a bit. 

When you ask about eating fast... I guess I'd have to admit that, yeah, I do. It's almost like I'm back on the road and on a really tight delivery schedule, you know? I just... I eat so fast I barely even taste what I'm having. Sometimes I'll catch myself actually breathing hard because I'm just shoveling it in without taking a second to slow down. 

I know that sounds terrible, and I really am trying to be more mindful about it. I just wanted to be completely honest with you since you asked again. Is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it's not very flattering.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I intentionally hide from people, doctor. I mean, my wife is usually around the house somewhere, and I don't lock the door or anything dramatic like that. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... I do usually wait until she's out running errands, or maybe working in the garden. It's not that I'm trying to be sneaky, I just... I know it wouldn't look good. She knows I'm trying to watch my weight with my bad back and all, and I just hate the idea of her seeing me like that, eating so much. I don't want to disappoint her, you know? 

So, yes, I suppose I do end up eating alone when it happens. I just want to keep the peace at home and not make a big deal out of it. Does that make sense? I hope that answers what you were asking.
During these overeating episodes, do you feel like you can't control yourself or stop eating once you start?

Well, doctor, I know we touched on this a little bit earlier, and I hope you don't mind me repeating myself... I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. 

But, yes, to answer your question directly... it really does feel like I can't stop. Like I said before, it's like all that discipline I had when I was driving just completely shuts off. It's the strangest thing. I'll literally be sitting there, in my own head, saying, 'Magin, put the fork down, you've had enough, you don't need this.' But... my hand just keeps going back for more. 

It's really hard to admit that out loud, because I've always prided myself on being in control of things. I hope you don't think I'm just making excuses for myself. I really am trying my best to get a handle on it. Is that... does that help explain what it feels like?

latest_inference.note: This turn confirmed the presence of a loss of control during overeating episodes, which is a key criterion for Binge Eating Disorder (F50.2). Other criteria such as eating more rapidly than normal, eating alone due to embarrassment, and significant distress were also endorsed. This rules out F50.9 (Unspecified Eating Disorder) as a primary diagnosis since enough specific symptoms are present to support F50.2.
